=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LogModel.md ===
# FEATURE: Log Model Attribution

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261024 V1 |
| Description | Attribute each decoded log record to its executed model, falling back to the requested model. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-LogDecode.md |
| Provides    | record model attribution |
| Consumes    | log record decoder |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Each record's model is the model that actually ran. When `result.stats.model` is present and non-empty it is used; otherwise the requested model `job.model` is used. The provider is read from `job.llm`, and an absent provider is the empty string. Reports group by this attribution, so it must be computed once per record, after decoding and before aggregation.

## Behavior

- Model = `result.stats.model` when that value is a string, present, and non-empty.
- Otherwise Model = `job.model`.
- Provider = `job.llm`; when absent, the empty string.
- Implemented as a pure function over one decoded record in `internal/logrecord`, returning `(provider, model string)`.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC log-model-prefers-executed ===
Intent: A record with a non-empty result.stats.model is attributed to that executed model.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import os

executed = "claude-haiku-5-5"
requested = "haiku"
record = {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "execution_id": "20261014.000000.000Z-aaaa0001",
    "started_at": "2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z",
    "status": "succeeded",
    "job": {"command_name": "build", "target": "T", "llm": "claude", "model": requested},
    "result": {"returncode": 0, "timed_out": False, "stats": {"model": executed}},
}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    path = os.path.join(d, "log.jsonl")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", "print('placeholder')"],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    print(result.stdout)
    print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert json.loads(json.dumps(record))["result"]["stats"]["model"] == executed
=== END AC log-model-prefers-executed ===

=== AC log-model-falls-back-to-requested ===
Intent: A record whose result.stats.model is absent or empty is attributed to job.model.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

import json

requested = "gpt-5.6-luna"
record = {
    "job": {"command_name": "plan", "target": "T", "llm": "codex", "model": requested},
    "result": {"stats": {"model": ""}},
}
assert record["result"]["stats"]["model"] == ""
assert record["job"]["model"] == requested
=== END AC log-model-falls-back-to-requested ===

=== AC log-model-absent-provider ===
Intent: A record with no job.llm is attributed an empty provider.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

record = {"job": {"command_name": "plan", "target": "T", "model": "haiku"}}
assert record["job"].get("llm", "") == ""
=== END AC log-model-absent-provider ===

# FEATURE: Log Numeric Stats

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261024 V1 |
| Description | Treat absent or null token, cost, and duration values as zero, and keep records with no stats object. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-LogDecode.md |
| Provides    | record numeric stats |
| Consumes    | log record decoder |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Token counts, cost, and duration are summed by every report. A value that is absent or `null` contributes zero. A record with no `result.stats` object is still a record and contributes zero to every numeric total.

## Behavior

- `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `elapsed_ms` are read as integers; absent or `null` is zero.
- `cost_usd` is read as float64; absent or `null` is zero.
- A record without `result.stats` yields all-zero numeric stats and is still counted.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC log-numeric-null-cost-is-zero ===
Intent: A cost_usd of null contributes zero to cost totals.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

record = {"result": {"stats": {"cost_usd": None, "input_tokens": 5}}}
cost = record["result"]["stats"].get("cost_usd")
total = float(cost) if cost is not None else 0.0
assert total == 0.0
=== END AC log-numeric-null-cost-is-zero ===

=== AC log-numeric-absent-tokens-are-zero ===
Intent: Absent token and duration fields are read as zero.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

record = {"result": {"stats": {"input_tokens": 7}}}
stats = record["result"]["stats"]
assert stats.get("output_tokens", 0) == 0
assert stats.get("cached_input_tokens", 0) == 0
assert stats.get("elapsed_ms", 0) == 0
assert stats["input_tokens"] == 7
=== END AC log-numeric-absent-tokens-are-zero ===

=== AC log-numeric-missing-stats-object ===
Intent: A record with no result.stats object is still a record with all-zero numeric stats.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

record = {"job": {"command_name": "plan"}, "result": {"returncode": 1}}
stats = record.get("result", {}).get("stats", {})
assert stats.get("input_tokens", 0) == 0
assert stats.get("cost_usd", 0) == 0
=== END AC log-numeric-missing-stats-object ===

# FEATURE: Target Filter

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261024 V1 |
| Description | Keep only records whose job.target equals the --target value exactly. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-LogDuplicates.md |
| Provides    | target filter |
| Consumes    | record stream after skip rules |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

The `--target` option narrows every report to records for one Target. The comparison is exact and case-sensitive. When the option is absent every record passes. The filter receives records only after the skip rules have run, so the whole-file `skipped` count is unaffected.

## Behavior

- With `--target X`, a record passes when `job.target == X` as a byte-exact string comparison.
- Without `--target`, every record passes.
- The filter never changes the skipped count.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC filter-target-exact-match ===
Intent: Only records whose job.target equals the requested name exactly pass the filter.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

def keep(record, target):
    return target is None or record["job"]["target"] == target

records = [
    {"job": {"target": "Toml"}},
    {"job": {"target": "toml"}},
    {"job": {"target": "Toml "}},
]
kept = [r for r in records if keep(r, "Toml")]
assert kept == [{"job": {"target": "Toml"}}]
=== END AC filter-target-exact-match ===

=== AC filter-target-absent-passes-all ===
Intent: When no target is given every record passes the filter.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

def keep(record, target):
    return target is None or record["job"]["target"] == target

records = [{"job": {"target": "A"}}, {"job": {"target": "B"}}]
assert [r for r in records if keep(r, None)] == records
=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Start Date Filter

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261024 V1 |
| Description | Keep records whose start date falls within the inclusive --since and --until range. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-FilterTarget.md |
| Provides    | date range filter |
| Consumes    | record stream after target filter |

## Questions

- Q-004: The source defines the start date as the first 10 characters of `started_at` but does not say what happens when that text is shorter than 10 characters or is not a date. System choice: use the first min(10, length) characters as the date text, and do not skip the record. This keeps the skip rules limited to the source's stated rules.

## Purpose

`--since` and `--until` keep records whose start date lies in an inclusive range. The start date is the first 10 characters of `started_at`. The CLI validates the option values before this filter runs.

## Behavior

- Start date = first `min(10, len(started_at))` characters of `started_at`.
- With `--since D`, keep records whose start date is greater than or equal to `D`.
- With `--until D`, keep records whose start date is less than or equal to `D`.
- Comparison is byte-wise on `YYYY-MM-DD` text, which orders the same as calendar dates.
- Options that are not given do not constrain the range.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC filter-date-inclusive-range ===
Intent: Records on the since and until boundaries are kept; records outside the range are dropped.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

def start_date(started_at):
    return started_at[:10]

def keep(record, since, until):
    d = start_date(record["started_at"])
    if since is not None and d < since:
        return False
    if until is not None and d > until:
        return False
    return True

records = [
    {"started_at": "2026-10-13T23:59:59.000Z"},
    {"started_at": "2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z"},
    {"started_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z"},
    {"started_at": "2026-10-16T00:00:00.000Z"},
    {"started_at": "2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z"},
]
kept = [r["started_at"] for r in records if keep(r, "2026-10-14", "2026-10-16")]
assert kept == [
    "2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z",
    "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z",
    "2026-10-16T00:00:00.000Z",
]
=== END AC filter-date-inclusive-range ===

=== AC filter-date-open-ended ===
Intent: Omitting one bound leaves the range open on that side.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

def start_date(started_at):
    return started_at[:10]

def keep(record, since, until):
    d = start_date(record["started_at"])
    if since is not None and d < since:
        return False
    if until is not None and d > until:
        return False
    return True

records = [
    {"started_at": "2026-10-13T00:00:00.000Z"},
    {"started_at": "2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z"},
]
assert [r for r in records if keep(r, "2026-10-14", None)] == [records[1]]
assert [r for r in records if keep(r, None, "2026-10-14")] == [records[0]]
=== END AC filter-date-open-ended ===

=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Report Formatting

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261024 V1 |
| Description | Provide the shared minutes formatter, the cost formatter, and the CSV writer used by every report. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |
| Provides    | FormatMinutes, FormatCost, WriteCSV |
| Consumes    | none |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Every report shares three output rules: minutes are written in tenths of a minute, cost is written with four decimal places, and rows are written as CSV with `\n` line endings. Centralising these keeps every report byte-consistent.

## Behavior

- `FormatMinutes(ms int64) string`: `t = (ms + 3000) / 6000` in integer division, written as `t/10`, a period, and `t%10`. For example `95000` ms writes `1.6`.
- `FormatCost(usd float64) string`: `fmt.Sprintf("%.4f", usd)`.
- `WriteCSV(w io.Writer, rows [][]string) error`: writes each row with `encoding/csv`, comma-separated, `\n` line endings.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC report-format-minutes-rounding ===
Intent: Minutes are written as tenths of a minute, rounded half up, so 95000 ms writes 1.6.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

def format_minutes(ms):
    t = (ms + 3000) // 6000
    return f"{t // 10}.{t % 10}"

assert format_minutes(95000) == "1.6"
assert format_minutes(0) == "0.0"
=== END AC report-format-minutes-rounding ===

=== AC report-format-cost-four-places ===
Intent: Cost is written with exactly four decimal places.
Requires: executable=python3; scope=test

usd = 5.5245
assert f"{usd:.4f}" == "5.5245"
assert f"{0.0:.4f}" == "0.0000"
=== END AC report-format-cost-four-places ===

=== END ARTIFACT ===
